Born global. Built to scale. Inclusive by design.

Three commitments, and what each one costs us

Born global

Hardtech cannot be built for one market. Canada Catalyst brings international founders in through Soft Landing and Start-Up Visa pathways, and partnerships run to Taiwan, Korea, Serbia, the UK, and the US Northeast semiconductor corridor.

Built to scale

We select for ventures that need instruments, not just desks. That means carrying $12 million of lab equipment and a $3 million AI compute lab, which is a heavier balance sheet than a coworking model would need.

Inclusive by design

Programs like Tech Undivided exist because a founder network left to itself reproduces itself. Certified as a Great Place to Work in 2022 and 2023, and recognised in Canada's Most Admired Corporate Cultures in 2024.

Industries of focus

Four sectors where Ontario can actually win

Research depth, manufacturing capacity, and a customer base within a day's drive. We concentrate on the four where all three are true at once.

Innovation Space

Most incubators offer desks. We offer instruments.

A 50,000 square foot facility in Markham with $12 million of hardware and testing labs and a $3 million AI compute lab. It is the reason a semiconductor founder can build here instead of shipping a prototype to California.

Home / Programs

Every program, side by side

ventureLAB runs seven programs for hardtech founders, from $10,000 in non-dilutive funding at the idea stage through to scaleup support. Each year over 100 ventures are selected.

Idea

You have a concept and need capital to reach a first build.

Pre-seed

You need instruments, benches, and technical advisors.

Seed to Series A

You need to be ready for institutional and angel capital.

Scale

You need new markets, customers, and industry standing.

How to apply

Four steps, about six weeks

1

Join an info session

ventureLAB runs regular sessions covering every program and who each one is for. No application needed to attend.

2

Submit an application

One form per program. Idea-stage founders in York Region should look at the Entrepreneurship and Innovation Fund first.

3

Meet the team

A conversation about the technology, the market, and what you actually need from a program rather than what sounds impressive.

4

Join a cohort

Over 100 ventures are selected each year. Cohorts run continuously, so a miss is a timing question rather than a verdict.

Timeline is illustrative for this prototype. The live site publishes program pages but not a single application path, which is one of the clearest gaps a founder hits.

Home / Portfolio / TransPod Inc.

TransPod Inc.

TransPod is a Toronto-based ventureLAB portfolio company developing an electric, ultra-high-speed passenger and freight transportation system.

About

TransPod develops ultra-high-speed vacuum-tube transportation systems and IntelliSense AI for structural health monitoring. Together, these technologies support rapid logistics mobility, resilient infrastructure, and predictive maintenance, enhancing mission readiness while reducing operating risk for the secure movement of critical equipment and personnel.

Dual-use potential

Ultra-high-speed transport supports rapid movement of equipment and personnel, strengthening logistics and mobility planning. IntelliSense AI enables predictive maintenance through vibration-based analytics, improving infrastructure resilience and asset safety. Digital twins and simulation tools support scenario testing, redundancy planning, and operational training for complex transport and defence systems.

What this page would publish

Nine filled fields become machine-readable markup. This is what a completed record emits, and it is what a retrieval system reads when someone asks which Ontario companies work on high-speed transport.

{
  "@type": "Organization",
  "name": "TransPod Inc.",
  "description": "Electric, ultra-high-speed passenger
     and freight transportation systems.",
  "location": "Toronto, Ontario, Canada",
  "memberOf": { "@type": "Organization",
                "name": "ventureLAB" },
  "knowsAbout": ["vacuum-tube transport",
                 "structural health monitoring"],
  "sameAs": ["https://transpod.com", "..."]
}

Why the greyed rows matter

ventureLAB publishes roughly 2,400 pages, and portfolio company pages are the largest set at 406 visible in the sitemap. Each is a page about a real organisation, which is the exact shape a retrieval system can quote.

Today those pages carry a name, a paragraph, and a link. No founding year, no stage, no cohort, no sameAs to LinkedIn or Crunchbase, and no Organization markup.

Filling nine fields per company turns a description into an entity, and turns 2,400 orphan pages into the most complete verified hardtech company dataset in Ontario.

    One address, everywhere

    The live site prints Room E171 in the header and Room C-106 in the footer of the same page, and quotes the labs as $11 million on portfolio pages and $12 million on the Innovation Space page.

    A person shrugs at that. A retrieval system treats it as conflicting facts about one organisation and gets less confident about quoting either.

    One canonical record, published once and referenced everywhere, is the cheapest correctness fix on the site. This prototype uses the newer figures throughout.
